To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NtWRKEY12 interacts with TGA2, and that this interaction is required for PR-1a expression.
NtWRXY12 interacts with TGA2 in vivo and in vitro and that this interaction might play a role in PR-1 gene expression.
NtWRK12 interacts with TGA2 in vitro and interacts with TGA1 in planta, and that this interaction is required for PR-1a expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of the tobacco transcription factors NtWRKY1, NtWRKY2, NtWRK12, NtWRKS1, NtNPR, NtTGA1a, NtTGB1, NtTGC1, NtTG2.1, NtTAG1, NtSIP1 and their interactions with other transcription factors and with the promoter of the salicilic acid-inducible tobacco PR-1a and Arab
the characterization of a WRKY transcription factor from tobacco that interacts in vitro and in living cells with a member of the TGA family of transcription factors.
the identification of a new transcriptional activator for the PR-1a promoter and the elucidation of the mechanism of its interaction with TGA2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NtWRXY12 and TGA factors can interact and that this interaction is necessary for the regulation of the PR-1a promoter.
the transcription factor NtNPR4 is able to bind to the as-1-like element of the NtPR-1a gene promoter in vitro and in planta.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NtWRK12 interacts with TGA2 in vitro and that this is also the case for NtWRKY2, NtWRKY3, and NtWRKY4.
the interaction of NtWRK12 with TGA2 is a prerequisite for PR-1a induction by SA and that the interaction of TGA2 with WRKY12 is a prerequisite for the interaction of WRKY12 with TGFs, such as TGA2.
the NtWRKY transcription factors NtWRKY11 and NtWRKY14 are negative regulators of salicylic acid-induced PR-1a expression, whereas NtWRKY1 and NtWRYK12 act as activators.

NtWRK12 and TGA 2.2 interact and this interaction may be responsible for the transcriptional activation of the PR-1a promoter.
